units.zh: 器甲之制
units.en: Regulations for Weapons and Armor
units.literal: Regulations for weapons and armor.

units.zh: 器甲之制，其工署則有南北作坊，有弓弩院，諸州皆有作院，皆役工徒而限其常課。
units.en: Under the regulations governing weapons and armor, craft offices included the Northern and Southern Workshops and the Bow and Crossbow Court, and every prefecture maintained its own manufacturing office, all employing artisans and laborers subject to fixed annual quotas.
units.literal: As for regulations for weapons and armor, the craft offices had the Northern and Southern Workshops and the Bow and Crossbow Court; every prefecture also had manufacturing offices, all employing artisans and laborers while fixing their regular quotas.

units.zh: 南北作坊歲造塗金脊鐵甲等凡三萬二千，弓弩院歲造角巴弓等凡千六百五十餘萬，諸州歲造黃樺、黑漆弓弩等凡六百二十餘萬。
units.en: Each year the Northern and Southern Workshops turned out thirty-two thousand pieces of gold-plated spine iron armor and similar gear; the Bow and Crossbow Court produced more than sixteen and a half million horn-backed bows and the like; and the prefectures produced more than six million two hundred thousand yellow birch and black-lacquered bows, crossbows, and similar items.
units.literal: The Northern and Southern Workshops annually produced thirty-two thousand gold-plated spine iron armor and the like; the Bow and Crossbow Court annually produced horn-backed bows and the like totaling more than sixteen million five hundred thousand; the prefectures annually produced yellow birch and black-lacquered bows, crossbows, and the like totaling more than six million two hundred thousand.

units.zh: 又南北作坊及諸州別造兵幕、甲袋、梭衫等什物，以備軍行之用。
units.en: The Northern and Southern Workshops and the prefectures also manufactured campaign gear such as military tents, armor bags, and padded armor shirts for use in the field.
units.literal: Moreover the Northern and Southern Workshops and the various prefectures separately made military tents, armor bags, padded armor shirts, and other sundries to supply use on campaign.

units.zh: 京師所造，十日一進，謂之「旬課」。
units.en: Products made in the capital were delivered every ten days in what was called the "ten-day quota."
units.literal: What was made in the capital was submitted every ten days, called the "ten-day quota."

units.zh: 上親閱視，置五庫以貯之。
units.en: The emperor personally inspected the output and established five storehouses to hold it.
units.literal: The emperor personally inspected them and established five storehouses to store them.

units.zh: 嘗令試床子弩於郊外，矢及七百步，又令別造步弩以試。
units.en: He once had a bed crossbow tested outside the city; its bolt flew seven hundred paces, and also ordered a separate foot crossbow built for trial.
units.literal: He once ordered a bed crossbow tested in the suburbs; the arrow reached seven hundred paces, and also ordered a separate foot crossbow made for trial.

units.zh: 戎具精致犀利，近代未有。
units.en: The arms and armor were exquisitely wrought and keen—unmatched in recent times.
units.literal: The military equipment was exquisitely refined and sharp; nothing like it in recent times.

units.zh: 開寶三年五月，詔：「京都士庶之家，不得私蓄兵器。
units.en: In the fifth month of the third year of Kaibao (970), an edict declared: "Households of scholars and commoners in the capital may not keep weapons in private stores.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Kaibao, an edict: "Households of gentry and commoners in the capital may not privately store weapons.

units.zh: 軍士素能自備技擊之器者，寄掌本軍之司；
units.en: Soldiers who habitually provided their own close-combat weapons were to lodge them with their unit's office;
units.literal: Soldiers who were accustomed to supplying their own skill-and-strike weapons were to deposit them with their army's office;

units.zh: 俟出征，則陳牒以請。
units.en: and when a campaign was imminent, they filed a petition to retrieve them.
units.literal: when about to go on campaign, they submitted a petition to request them.

units.zh: 品官準法聽得置隨身器械。」
units.en: Officials of rank were allowed by statute to keep personal arms on their persons."
units.literal: Ranked officials were permitted by regulation to keep personal sidearms."

units.zh: 時兵部令史馮繼升等進火箭法，命試驗，且賜衣物、束帛。
units.en: At that time Feng Jisheng and other clerks of the Ministry of War presented a method for fire arrows; they were ordered to demonstrate it and were rewarded with clothing and silks.
units.literal: At that time Ministry of War clerks Feng Jisheng and others presented the fire-arrow method; they were ordered to test it and were also granted clothing and silks.

units.zh: 淳化二年，申明不得私蓄兵器之禁。
units.en: In the second year of Chunhua (991), the ban on private possession of weapons was reaffirmed.
units.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, the prohibition on privately storing weapons was clarified anew.

units.zh: 至道二年二月，詔：先造光明細鋼甲以給士卒者，初無襯裏，宜以紬裏之，俾擐者不磨傷肌體。
units.en: In the second month of the second year of Zhidao (996), an edict ordered that the bright fine steel armor first made for troops, which originally had no lining, should be lined with silk so that wearers would not abrade their skin.
units.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhidao, an edict: Those who had first made bright fine steel armor for soldiers had originally had no lining; it should be lined with silk so that those who don it would not chafe their flesh.

units.zh: 咸平元年六月，御前忠佐石歸宋獻木羽弩箭，箭裁尺餘，而所激甚遠，中鎧甲則竿去而鏃存，牢不可拔。詔增歸宋月奉，且補其子為東西班侍。
units.en: In the sixth month of the first year of Xianping (998), Palace-front Loyal Associate Shi Gui-Song presented wooden-feathered crossbow bolts barely more than a foot long that nonetheless flew very far; when they struck armor the shaft fell away while the point remained lodged and could not be pulled free. An edict raised Gui-Song's monthly stipend and appointed his son as an Eastern and Western Class attendant.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Xianping, Palace-front Loyal Associate Shi Gui-Song presented wooden-feathered crossbow bolts; the bolts were barely more than a foot long, yet when shot they flew very far, and when they struck armor the shaft fell away while the point remained, fixed so firmly it could not be pulled out. An edict increased Gui-Song's monthly stipend and also appointed his son as an Eastern and Western Class attendant.

units.zh: 三年四月，神騎副兵馬使焦偓獻盤鐵槊，重十五斤，令偓試之，馬上往復如飛，命遷本軍使。
units.en: In the fourth month of the third year (1000), Jiao Wo, vice horse-and-arms commander of the Shenqi Army, presented coiled iron spears weighing fifteen jin; ordered to demonstrate them, he wheeled about on horseback as if flying, and was promoted to command that army.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, Shenqi Vice Horse-and-Arms Commander Jiao Wo presented coiled iron spears weighing fifteen jin; he was ordered to test them, and on horseback they went back and forth like flying; he was ordered promoted to command that army.

units.zh: 八月，神衛水軍隊長唐福獻所製火箭、火球、火蒺藜，造船務匠項綰等獻海戰船式，各賜緡錢。
units.en: In the eighth month, Tang Fu, formation leader of the Shenwei Naval Army, presented designs for rockets, fire balls, and fire caltrops; shipyard craftsmen Xiang Wan and others presented models of warships, and each party received cash rewards.
units.literal: In the eighth month, Shenwei Naval Formation Leader Tang Fu presented rocket, fire ball, and fire caltrop designs; Shipyard craftsmen Xiang Wan and others presented naval battle-ship models, each receiving cash rewards.

units.zh: 先是，相國寺僧法山，本洺州人，強姓，其族百口，悉為戎人所掠。
units.en: Earlier, the monk Fashan of Xiangguo Temple, a native of Mingzhou surnamed Qiang, had seen his clan of one hundred persons all seized by the barbarians.
units.literal: Earlier, the monk Fashan of Xiangguo Temple, a native of Mingzhou of the surname Qiang, his clan of one hundred mouths—all were carried off by the barbarians.

units.zh: 至是，願還俗隸軍伍以效死力，且獻鐵輪撥，渾重三十三斤，首尾有刃，為馬上格戰具。
units.en: Now he wished to leave the clergy, enlist, and fight to the death, and presented an iron wheel stirrer weighing thirty-three jin, bladed at both ends, as a weapon for mounted melee.
units.literal: At this time he wished to return to lay life and join the army to offer his strength unto death, and presented an iron wheel stirrer, ponderous at thirty-three jin, with blades at head and tail, as equipment for mounted close combat.

units.zh: 詔補外殿直。
units.en: He was appointed an Outer Palace Duty Attendant by edict.
units.literal: He was ordered appointed Outer Palace Duty Attendant.

units.zh: 五年，知寧化軍劉永錫製手炮以獻，詔沿邊造之以充用。
units.en: In the fifth year (1002), Liu Yongxi, commissioner of Ninghua Army, devised a hand cannon and presented it; the court ordered the border commands to build them for service.
units.literal: In the fifth year, Liu Yongxi, military commissioner of Ninghua Army, made hand cannon and presented it; an edict ordered the border regions to manufacture them for use.

units.zh: 六年十月，給軍中傳信牌。
units.en: In the tenth month of the sixth year (1003), message tokens were issued to the army.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year, message tokens were issued to the army.

units.zh: 其制，漆木為牌，長六寸，闊三寸，腹背刻字而中分之，置鑿枘令可合；
units.en: They were made of lacquered wood, six inches long and three inches wide, with characters carved on both faces and split down the middle, fitted with mortise and tenon so the halves could join;
units.literal: Their design: lacquered wood for the token, six inches long and three inches wide, characters carved on front and back and split down the middle, with mortise and tenon so they could join;

units.zh: 又穿二竅容筆墨，上施紙劄。
units.en: and two holes bored to hold brush and ink, with paper slips attached above.
units.literal: Also two holes bored to hold brush and ink, with paper slips attached on top.

units.zh: 每臨陣則分而持之，或傳令，則署其言而係軍吏之頸，至彼合契，乃書復命。
units.en: In battle each side kept half; to pass an order, the sender inscribed the message and tied the token to a clerk's neck; when the recipient matched the tally, he wrote the reply.
units.literal: On each battle they split and held them; when transmitting orders, they signed their words and tied them to a military clerk's neck; when the other party matched the tally, they wrote the reply.

units.zh: 因冀州團練使石普之請也。
units.en: This followed a request from Shi Pu, militia commissioner of Jizhou.
units.literal: This was at the request of Jizhou Militia Commissioner Shi Pu.

units.zh: 仁宗時，天下久不用兵。
units.en: Under Emperor Renzong, the empire had long been at peace.
units.literal: During the time of Emperor Renzong, the realm had long gone without war.

units.zh: 天聖四年，詔減諸路歲造兵器之半。
units.en: In the fourth year of Tiansheng (1026), an edict cut annual weapons production on every circuit by half.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tiansheng, an edict halved the annual weapons production of the various circuits.

units.zh: 是歲，詔作坊造鐵槍一萬五千，給秦、渭、環、慶、延州、鎮戎軍。
units.en: That same year, workshops were ordered to forge fifteen thousand iron spears for Qin, Wei, Huan, Qing, Yanzhou, and Zhenrong Army.
units.literal: That year, an edict ordered the workshops to make fifteen thousand iron spears and supply Qin, Wei, Huan, Qing, Yanzhou, and Zhenrong Army.

units.zh: 六年，詔：外器甲久不繕，先遣使分詣諸路閱視修治之。
units.en: In the sixth year (1028), an edict noted that arms and armor in the field had long gone unmaintained and sent envoys to each circuit to inspect and repair them.
units.literal: In the sixth year, an edict: outer weapons and armor long unrepaired—first dispatch envoys to each circuit to inspect and repair them.

units.zh: 景祐二年，罷秦州造輸京師弓弩三年。
units.en: In the second year of Jingyou (1035), Qinzhou was relieved for three years of its obligation to ship bows and crossbows to the capital.
units.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, the practice of Qinzhou manufacturing bows and crossbows for delivery to the capital was suspended for three years.

units.zh: 詔：「廣南民家毋得置博刀，犯者並鍛人並以私有禁兵律論。」
units.en: An edict declared: "Households in Guangnan may not keep broad knives; offenders and the smith who forged them shall be punished under the law against private possession of prohibited arms."
units.literal: An edict: "Households in Guangnan may not keep broad knives; violators and the smith who forged them alike shall be prosecuted under the statute on privately possessing prohibited weapons."

units.zh: 先是，嶺南為盜者多持博刀，杖罪輕，不能禁，轉運使以為言，故著是令。
units.en: Bandits in the far south had often carried broad knives, but the light bamboo-staff penalty failed to deter them; the transport commissioner raised the issue, and this rule was therefore promulgated.
units.literal: Earlier, many bandits in Lingnan carried broad knives; the bamboo-staff penalty was light and could not restrain them; the transport commissioner reported this, hence this order was issued.

units.zh: 四年，詔作坊製栓子槍、柧槍各五萬。
units.en: In the fourth year (1037), workshops were ordered to produce fifty thousand bolt spears and fifty thousand shaft spears.
units.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered the workshops to make fifty thousand bolt spears and fifty thousand shaft spears.

units.zh: 康定元年四月，詔江南、淮南州軍造紙甲三萬，給陝西防城弓手。
units.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Kangding (1040), Jiangnan and Huainan commands were ordered to make thirty thousand suits of paper armor for Shaanxi wall-defense bowmen.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Kangding, an edict ordered Jiangnan and Huainan prefectures and armies to make thirty thousand paper armor for Shaanxi wall-defense bowmen.

units.zh: 又詔河東強壯習弩者聽自置，戶四等以下官給之。
units.en: Another edict allowed able men in Hedong trained with crossbows to arm themselves; for households below the fourth tax rank, the state would supply the weapons.
units.literal: Another edict: strong men in Hedong skilled with crossbows were permitted to supply their own; for households of the fourth rank and below, the government would provide them.

units.zh: 八月，詔陝西製柳木旁牌。
units.en: In the eighth month, Shaanxi was ordered to manufacture willowwood side shields.
units.literal: In the eighth month, an edict ordered Shaanxi to make willow side shields.

units.zh: 慶曆元年，知并州楊偕遣陽曲縣主簿楊拯獻《龍虎八陣圖》及所製神盾、劈陣刀、手刀、鐵連槌、鐵簡，且言《龍虎八陣圖》有奇有正，有進有止，遠則射，近則擊以刀盾。
units.en: In the first year of Qingli (1041), Yang Jie, prefect of Bingzhou, sent Yang Zheng, registrar of Yangqu County, to present the Dragon-Tiger Eight Formations Diagram together with his inventions—the divine shield, formation-splitting saber, hand saber, iron linked mace, and iron rod—and argued that the formation combined orthodox and unorthodox movements, advance and halt: shoot at range, strike with blade and shield at close quarters.
units.literal: In the first year of Qingli, Yang Jie, prefect of Bingzhou, sent Yangqu County Registrar Yang Zheng to present the "Dragon-Tiger Eight Formations Diagram" and his inventions—the divine shield, formation-splitting blade, hand blade, iron linked mace, and iron rod—and stated that the diagram had odd and even, advance and halt; at distance shoot, at close strike with blade and shield.

units.zh: 彼蕃騎雖眾，見神盾之異，必遽奔潰，然後以驍騎夾擊，無不勝者。
units.en: Though enemy cavalry might be numerous, once they saw the divine shield they would break and flee; crack horsemen could then strike from both flanks and victory would be assured.
units.literal: Though the barbarian cavalry were many, seeing the divine shield's strangeness they would surely flee in rout; then use crack cavalry to strike from both sides—none could fail to win.

units.zh: 歷代用兵，未有經慮及此。
units.en: No previous age of warfare, he claimed, had ever been planned with such care.
units.literal: In warfare through the ages, none had ever planned to this degree.

units.zh: 帝閱於崇政殿，降詔獎諭。
units.en: The emperor reviewed the designs in Chongzheng Hall and issued a commendatory edict.
units.literal: The emperor reviewed them in Chongzheng Hall and issued an edict of commendation.

units.zh: 其後，言者以為其器重大，緩急難用云。
units.en: Later critics judged the gear too heavy to be practical in a crisis.
units.literal: Later, critics said the weapons were heavy and hard to use in emergencies.

units.zh: 二年，詔鄜延、環慶、涇原、秦鳳路各置都作院，賜河北義勇兵弓弩箭材各一百萬。
units.en: In the second year (1042), each of the Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, and Qinfeng circuits was ordered to establish a directorate manufacturing office, and Hebei's volunteer militia received one million units each of bow, crossbow, and arrow materials.
units.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered each of the Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, and Qinfeng circuits to establish a Directorate Manufacturing Office, and granted Hebei volunteer militia bow, crossbow, and arrow materials of one million each.

units.zh: 四年，賜鄜延路總管風羽子弩箭三十萬。
units.en: In the fourth year (1044), the Fuyan circuit commander received thirty thousand wind-feather bolt crossbow arrows.
units.literal: In the fourth year, thirty thousand wind-feather bolt crossbow arrows were granted to the Fuyan circuit commander.

units.zh: 五年，詔諸路所儲兵械悉報三司，三司歲具須知以聞，仍約為程式預頒之。
units.en: In the fifth year (1045), every circuit was ordered to report its stored arms to the State Finance Commission, which annually compiled requirements for the throne and issued standard patterns in advance.
units.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered every circuit to report all stored military gear to the State Finance Commission; the commission each year compiled requirements and reported, and also drew up models to distribute in advance.

units.zh: 八年，詔：「士庶之家所藏兵器，非法所許者，限一月送官。
units.en: In the eighth year (1048), an edict declared: "Arms held by scholars and commoners without legal authorization must be surrendered to the government within one month.
units.literal: In the eighth year, an edict: "Weapons kept in gentry and commoner households that the law does not permit must be delivered to the authorities within one month.

units.zh: 敢匿，聽人告捕。」
units.en: Anyone who conceals them may be reported and arrested."
units.literal: Those who dare conceal them—informants may report and seize them."

units.zh: 皇祐元年，御崇政殿，閱知澧州、供備庫副使宋守信所獻衝陣無敵流星弩、拒馬皮竹牌、火鎌石火綱三刃、黑漆順水山字鐵甲、野戰拒馬刀弩、砦腳車、衝陣劍輪無敵車、大風翎弩箭八種。
units.en: In the first year of Huangyou (1049), the emperor reviewed at Chongzheng Hall eight weapons presented by Song Shouxin, acting prefect of Li prefecture and vice commissioner of the Equipment Reserve Bureau: the Formation-Invincible Meteor Crossbow, barricade horsehide bamboo shields, fire sickle stone fire-net triple blades, black-lacquer current-following mountain-character iron armor, field-battle barricade blades and crossbows, stockade-leg carts, Formation Sword-Wheel Invincible Carts, and Great-Wind feathered crossbow bolts.
units.literal: In the first year of Huangyou, at Chongzheng Hall the emperor reviewed eight kinds of weapons presented by Song Shouxin, acting prefect of Li prefecture and vice commissioner of the Equipment Reserve Bureau: the Formation-Invincible Meteor Crossbow, barricade horsehide bamboo shields, fire sickle stone fire-net triple blades, black-lacquer current-following mountain-character iron armor, field-battle barricade horse blades and crossbows, stockade-leg carts, Formation Sword-Wheel Invincible Carts, and Great-Wind feathered crossbow bolts.

units.zh: 四年，河北、河東、陝西都總管司言：「郭諮所造獨轅衝陣無敵流星弩，可以備軍陣之用。」
units.en: In the fourth year (1052), the frontier headquarters of Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi reported: "Guo Zi's single-frame Formation-Invincible Meteor Crossbow is fit for use in battle lines."
units.literal: In the fourth year, the frontier command headquarters of Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi reported: "Guo Zi's single-frame formation-invincible meteor crossbow can supply use in army formations."

units.zh: 詔弓弩院如樣製之。
units.en: The Bow and Crossbow Court was ordered to copy the design.
units.literal: An edict ordered the Bow and Crossbow Court to manufacture according to the model.

units.zh: 除諮為鄜延路鈐轄，許置弩五百，募土民教之。
units.en: Guo Zi was made deputy commissioner on the Fuyan circuit, allowed five hundred crossbows, and authorized to recruit locals to train crews.
units.literal: Guo Zi was appointed Fuyan circuit deputy commissioner, permitted to deploy five hundred crossbows, and recruit local men to train them.

units.zh: 既成，經略夏安期言其便，詔立獨轅弩軍。
units.en: When the weapons were ready, frontier commissioner Xia Anqi praised their utility, and an edict created the Single-Frame Crossbow Army.
units.literal: When completed, frontier commissioner Xia Anqi said they were convenient; an edict established the Single-Frame Crossbow Army.

units.zh: 五年，荊南兵馬鈐轄王遂上臨陣柺槍。
units.en: In the fifth year (1053), Wang Sui, military commissioner of Jingnan, presented a battle crutch spear.
units.literal: In the fifth year, Jingnan Military Commissioner Wang Sui presented a battle crutch spear.

units.zh: 至和元年，詔河北、河東、陝西路每歲夏曝器甲，有損斷者，悉令完備。
units.en: In the first year of Zhihe (1054), the Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits were ordered each summer to air weapons and armor in the sun and repair every damaged piece.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, an edict ordered the Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi circuits each summer to sun-dry weapons and armor; any damaged or broken items were to be fully repaired.

units.zh: 如復閱視有不堪用者，知州、通判並主兵官並貶秩。
units.en: If reinspection still found gear unfit for use, the prefect, vice-prefect, and military commanders were all demoted.
units.literal: If on re-inspection any were still unusable, the prefect, vice-prefect, and commanding military officers alike were demoted in rank.

units.zh: 嘉祐四年，詔京師所製軍器，多不鋒利，其選朝臣、使臣各一員揀試之。
units.en: In the fourth year of Jiayou (1059), an edict noted that arms made in the capital were often dull and ordered one court official and one imperial envoy each to test and grade them.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Jiayou, an edict: weapons made in the capital were mostly not sharp; select one court official and one envoy each to test and sort them.

units.zh: 七年，詔江西制置賊盜司，在所有私造兵甲匠並籍姓名，若再犯者，並妻子徙淮南。
units.en: In the seventh year (1062), the Jiangxi Bandit-Suppression Office was told to register every private armorer by name; repeat offenders and their families were exiled to Huainan.
units.literal: In the seventh year, an edict to the Jiangxi Bandit-Suppression Office: register by name all private armorers in each prefecture; repeat offenders and their wives and children were exiled to Huainan.

units.zh: 熙寧元年，始命入內副都知張若水、西上閣門使李評料簡弓弩而增修之。
units.en: In the first year of Xining (1068), Zhang Ruoshui, deputy director of the inner service, and Li Ping, western upper gate commissioner, were first assigned to review and upgrade bows and crossbows.
units.literal: In the first year of Xining, Zhang Ruoshui, Deputy Director of the Inner Service, and Li Ping, Western Upper Gate Commissioner, were first ordered to sort through bows and crossbows and improve them.

units.zh: 若水進所造神臂弓，實李宏所獻，蓋弩類也。
units.en: Ruoshui presented the "divine-arm" crossbow he had devised—it had actually been submitted by Li Hong and belonged to the crossbow family.
units.literal: Ruoshui presented the divine-arm crossbow he had made—it was actually submitted by Li Hong and was a type of crossbow.

units.zh: 以檿為身，檀為肖，鐵為鐙子槍頭，銅為馬麵牙發，麻繩紥絲為弦。
units.en: Its stock was mulberry wood, its prods sandalwood, its stirrup-shaped spearhead iron, its horse-face release bronze, and its string hemp cord bound with silk.
units.literal: Mulberry for the stock, sandalwood for the prods, iron for the stirrup-shaped spearhead, copper for the horse-face release, hemp cord bound with silk for the string.

units.zh: 弓之身三尺有二寸，弦長二尺有五寸，箭木羽長數寸，射三百四十餘步，入榆木半笴。
units.en: The bow measured three feet two inches, the string two feet five; the bolt's shaft and fletching only a few inches. It shot more than three hundred forty paces and drove half a shaft into elm.
units.literal: The bow body was three feet two inches, the string two feet five inches; the arrow shaft and feathers a few inches; it shot more than three hundred forty paces and buried half a shaft in elm wood.

units.zh: 帝閱而善之。
units.en: The emperor inspected it and approved.
units.literal: The emperor reviewed it and approved.

units.zh: 於是神臂始用，而他器弗及焉。
units.en: The divine-arm crossbow then entered service, and no other weapon could rival it.
units.literal: Thereupon the divine-arm [crossbow] began to be used, and no other weapon matched it.

units.zh: 二年，命河北州軍凡戎器分三等以聞，又詔內庫凡器甲擇其良若干條上。
units.en: In the second year (1069), every Hebei command was ordered to classify its arms in three grades; the inner storehouse was also told to select the finest specimens of each armor and weapon type and submit specifications.
units.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered every Hebei prefecture and army to report military gear in three grades; another edict ordered the inner storehouse to select the best of each type of armor and weapons and submit specifications.

units.zh: 四年，詔諸路遣官詣州，分庫藏甲兵器為三等如沿邊三路，而川峽不與。
units.en: In the fourth year (1071), envoys were sent to classify depot armor and weapons in three grades as on the frontier circuits, excluding Sichuan and the gorges.
units.literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered officials sent to each prefecture to divide stored armor and weapons in storehouses into three grades as on the three frontier circuits, but Sichuan and the gorges were excluded.

units.zh: 五年，帝匣斬馬刀以示蔡挺，挺謂製作精而操擊便，乃命中人領工造數萬口賜邊臣，鐔長尺餘，刃三尺餘，首為大環。
units.en: In the fifth year (1072), the emperor displayed a horse-slaying saber to Cai Ting, who praised its craftsmanship and ease of use; eunuchs were ordered to supervise tens of thousands for frontier commanders—the guard over a foot long, the blade over three feet, with a large ring pommel.
units.literal: In the fifth year, the emperor took out a horse-slaying saber to show Cai Ting; Ting said the workmanship was fine and the handling convenient; the emperor then ordered eunuchs to supervise manufacture of tens of thousands to grant frontier officials—the guard a foot odd, the blade three feet odd, the pommel a large ring.

units.zh: 是歲，詔權三司度支副使沈起詳定軍器制度。
units.en: That year Shen Qi, acting vice commissioner of revenue, was ordered to codify regulations for military equipment.
units.literal: That year, an edict ordered Acting Vice Commissioner of Revenue Shen Qi to fix regulations for military equipment.

units.zh: 起以為一己之見有限，宜令在京及三路主兵官、監官、工匠審度法度所宜，庶可傳久。
units.en: Qi argued that a single opinion was too narrow and proposed that military officers, supervisors, and craftsmen in the capital and on the three frontier circuits jointly determine standards that would endure.
units.literal: Qi thought one man's view was limited; it was fitting to have frontier and capital military officers, supervisors, and craftsmen in the three circuits assess what the regulations should be, so they could be handed down long.

units.zh: 詔從之。
units.en: The emperor approved.
units.literal: An edict approved this.

units.zh: 時帝欲利戎器，而患有司苟簡。
units.en: The emperor then sought better arms but worried that officials would be slipshod.
units.literal: At that time the emperor wished to improve military gear but feared the responsible offices would be perfunctory.

units.zh: 王雱上疏曰：「漢宣帝號中興賢主，而史稱技巧工匠，獨精於元、成之時。
units.en: Wang Pang submitted a memorial: "Emperor Xuan of Han is hailed as a restorative ruler, yet histories say skilled artisans flourished only under Emperors Yuan and Cheng.
units.literal: Wang Pang submitted a memorial saying: "Emperor Xuan of Han was called a worthy ruler of restoration, yet the histories say that skilled craftsmen excelled only in the times of Emperors Yuan and Cheng.

units.zh: 是雖有司之事，而上係朝廷之政。
units.en: Though this is ostensibly an administrative matter, it reflects court policy from above.
units.literal: Though this is the affair of responsible offices, above it is tied to court policy.

units.zh: 方今外禦邊患，內虞盜賊，而天下歲課弓弩、甲胄入充武庫者以千萬數，乃無一堅好精利實可為備者。
units.en: Today the empire faces border threats abroad and bandits within, yet millions of bows, crossbows, and armor enter the arsenal each year without a single piece stout, keen, and truly serviceable.
units.literal: Now we defend the frontier without and guard against bandits within, yet the annual quota of bows, crossbows, and armor entering the arsenal runs to tens of millions—yet not one piece is stout, fine, sharp, and truly fit to be kept in reserve.

units.zh: 臣嘗觀諸州作院兵匠乏少，至拘市人以備役，所作之器，但形質而已。
units.en: I have seen prefectural workshops short of armorer-soldiers, conscripting townspeople to meet quotas and turning out mere shells of weapons.
units.literal: Your servant has observed that in many prefectures the manufacturing offices lack armorer-soldiers and even seize townspeople to fill quotas; what they make is mere outward form.

units.zh: 武庫之吏，計其多寡之數而藏之，未嘗責其實用，故所積雖多，大抵敝惡。
units.en: Arsenal clerks count pieces for the ledger and never test them; stores are vast but mostly worthless.
units.literal: Arsenal clerks count numbers for storage and never demand practical use; thus though accumulated stores are many, they are mostly worn and bad.

units.zh: 夫為政如此，而欲抗威決勝，外攘內修，未見其可也。
units.en: With governance like this, to project power, win battles, and secure the realm inside and out seems impossible.
units.literal: To govern thus yet hope to display might, decide victory, repel outsiders and repair within—this is not yet seen as possible.

units.zh: 儻欲弛武備，示天下以無事，則金木、絲枲、筋膠、角羽之材，皆民力也，無故聚工以毀之，甚可惜也。
units.en: If the court means to relax defenses and signal peace, the gold, timber, silk, sinew, glue, horn, and feather that go into arms are all drawn from the people's labor; gathering craftsmen only to ruin the product is a grievous waste.
units.literal: If one wishes to relax military preparedness and show the realm there is no trouble, then gold, wood, silk, hemp, sinew, glue, horn, and feather materials are all the people's labor; to gather craftsmen without cause to destroy them is deeply regrettable.

units.zh: 莫若更製法度，斂數州之作聚為一處，若今錢監之比，擇知工事之臣使專其職；
units.en: Better to revise the rules, consolidate several prefectures' workshops as with mints, and appoint officials who understand craft to oversee them;
units.literal: Better to remake regulations, gather several prefectures' production into one place as with coin foundries today, select officials who understand the work to specialize in it;

units.zh: 且募天下良工散為匠師，而朝廷內置工官以總制其事，察其精窳而賞罰之，則人人務勝，不加責而皆精矣。
units.en: recruit skilled artisans from across the empire as masters while inner craft officials supervise, rewarding excellence and punishing shoddy work—then all will strive for quality without further coercion.
units.literal: and recruit the realm's fine craftsmen as master artisans while the court places craft officials within to oversee, inspecting fineness and coarseness for reward and punishment—then each will strive to excel, and without extra demands all will be refined.

units.zh: 聞今武庫太祖時弓尚有如新者，而近世所造往往不可用，此可見法禁之張弛矣。」
units.en: Bows from Taizu's reign in the arsenal are said to remain like new, while recent products often fail—proof of how discipline has slackened."
units.literal: It is heard that in the arsenal bows from Taizu's time are still like new, while those made in recent times are often unusable—this shows how tight or loose the regulations have been."

units.zh: 大抵雱為此言，以迎逢上意，欲妄更舊制也。
units.en: In sum, Pang's argument catered to the emperor's mood and sought rashly to overturn established practice.
units.literal: In general An spoke thus to court the emperor's wishes, wishing rashly to overturn the old system.

units.zh: 六年，始置軍器監，總內外軍器之政。
units.en: In the sixth year (1073), the Directorate of Military Equipment was established to govern all arms production.
units.literal: In the sixth year, the Directorate of Military Equipment was first established to oversee all military gear within and without.

units.zh: 置判一人、同判一人。
units.en: It was staffed with one director and one associate director.
units.literal: One director and one associate director were appointed.

units.zh: 屬有丞，有主簿，有管當公事。
units.en: Subordinates included vice directors, registrars, and routine clerks.
units.literal: Subordinate to it were vice directors, registrars, and officials in charge of routine business.

units.zh: 先是，軍器領於三司，至是罷之，一總於監。
units.en: Formerly arms had been managed by the State Finance Commission; that role ended and authority passed to the directorate.
units.literal: Earlier military equipment had been under the State Finance Commission; now that was abolished and everything unified under the directorate.

units.zh: 凡產材州，置都作院。
units.en: Every material-producing prefecture gained a directorate manufacturing office.
units.literal: Every prefecture that produced materials established a directorate manufacturing office.

units.zh: 凡知軍器利害者，聽詣監陳述，於是吏民獻器械法式者甚眾。
units.en: Anyone knowledgeable about arms might petition the directorate, and officials and commoners flooded it with new designs.
units.literal: Whoever knew the advantages and harms of military equipment was permitted to report to the directorate; thereupon officials and commoners presenting weapon patterns were very many.

units.zh: 是歲，又置內弓箭南庫。
units.en: That year also saw the inner southern bow and crossbow depot.
units.literal: That year, the inner southern bow and crossbow depot was also established.

units.zh: 軍器監奏以利器頒諸路作院為式。
units.en: The directorate memorialized distributing superior weapons to circuit workshops as patterns.
units.literal: The Directorate of Military Equipment memorialized distributing fine weapons to circuit workshops as models.

units.zh: 是年冬，以騎兵據大鞍不便野戰，始製小鞍，皮韉木鐙，長於回旋，馬射得以馳驟，且選邊人習騎者分隸諸軍。
units.en: That winter, because horsemen on heavy saddles fought poorly in the field, lighter saddles with leather pads and wooden stirrups were introduced for quicker turns; mounted archers could charge freely, and frontier riders were drafted into the armies.
units.literal: That winter, because cavalry on large saddles were ill-suited to field battle, small saddles were first made with leather saddle blankets and wooden stirrups, better for turning; mounted archery could charge and wheel, and frontier men skilled in riding were selected and assigned to the various armies.

units.zh: 時周士隆上書論廣西、交阯事，請為車以禦象陣，文彥博非之。
units.en: Zhou Shilong then memorialized on Guangxi and Jiaozhi, proposing war chariots against elephant formations; Wen Yanbo objected.
units.literal: At that time Zhou Shilong memorialized on Guangxi and Jiaozhi affairs, asking for chariots to counter elephant formations; Wen Yanbo opposed this.

units.zh: 安石以為自前代至本朝，南方數以象勝中國，士隆策宜可用，因論自古車戰法甚辨，請以車騎相當試，以觀其孰利。
units.en: Wang Anshi argued that since antiquity the south had repeatedly beaten Chinese armies with elephants and that Shilong's plan deserved trial; he also expounded classical chariot doctrine and proposed a chariot-versus-cavalry test.
units.literal: An Shi thought that from former ages to the present dynasty the south had several times defeated China with elephants; Shilong's plan should be usable; he also argued ancient chariot warfare very persuasively and asked to test chariot against cavalry to see which was advantageous.

units.zh: 帝亦謂北邊地平，可用車為營，乃詔試車法，令沿河采車材三千兩，軍器監定法式，造戰車以進。
units.en: The emperor added that the northern plains suited chariot encampments; chariot tactics were ordered tested, three thousand cartloads of timber gathered along the rivers, the directorate to set patterns, and war chariots built for review.
units.literal: The emperor also said the northern frontier was level and chariots could form camps; an edict ordered chariot methods tested, three thousand cartloads of timber collected along the rivers, the directorate to fix the pattern, and battle chariots made and presented.

units.zh: 七年，判監呂惠卿言：「其所上弓式及其他兵器制度，下殿前、馬、步三司令定奪去取。
units.en: In the seventh year (1074), Director Lü Huiqing reported: "Bow patterns and other regulations I submitted were sent to the Palace, Horse, and Foot directorates for approval.
units.literal: In the seventh year, Director Lü Huiqing said: "The bow patterns and other weapon regulations I submitted were sent to the Palace, Horse, and Foot directorates for approval or rejection.

units.zh: 而逐司不過取責軍校文狀以聞，非獨持其舊說不肯更張，又其智慮未必能知作器之意。
units.en: But each bureau merely collected written opinions from training officers—not only clinging to old ways, they may not have understood weapon design at all.
units.literal: Yet each bureau merely took written statements from military school officers and reported them; not only did they cling to old views and refuse change, their wisdom may not have grasped the meaning of making weapons.

units.zh: 臣於朝廷已行之令，非敢言改，乞就一司同議。」
units.en: I dare not challenge edicts already promulgated; I ask only that one bureau deliberate with me."
units.literal: Regarding edicts already in force at court, I dare not speak of changing them; I beg to deliberate together in one bureau."

units.zh: 帝乃遣管軍郝質赴監定奪，皆曰「便」。
units.en: The emperor sent army supervisor Hao Zhi to the directorate to decide; all pronounced the designs "serviceable."
units.literal: The emperor then sent Army Supervisor Hao Zhi to the directorate for approval; all said "convenient."

units.zh: 時軍器監製器不一，材用滋耗。
units.en: Meanwhile the directorate produced arms without standardization, wasting ever more material.
units.literal: At that time the Directorate of Military Equipment made weapons without uniformity and materials were increasingly wasted.

units.zh: 於是詔不以常制選官馳往州縣根括牛皮角筋，能令數羨，次第加獎。
units.en: An edict then sent specially chosen officials to scour prefectures for ox hide, horn, and sinew, rewarding those who exceeded quotas.
units.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered officials selected outside the regular roster to hurry to prefectures and counties to root out ox hide, horn, and sinew; those who increased the tallies were rewarded in ascending order.

units.zh: 是歲，始造箭曰狼牙，曰鴨觜，曰出尖四楞，曰一插刃鑿子，凡四種推行之。
units.en: That year four new arrow types were introduced—the wolf's tooth, duck's bill, projecting four-angled, and one-insertion chisel blade—and put into general use.
units.literal: That year, arrows were first made called wolf's tooth, duck's bill, projecting four-angled, and one-insertion chisel blade—four kinds in all were promulgated.

units.zh: 八年，詔：「河北拒馬，或多以竹為之，不足當敵。
units.en: In the eighth year (1075), an edict declared: "Hebei abatis, often made of bamboo, cannot hold the enemy.
units.literal: In the eighth year, an edict: "Hebei abatis, many made of bamboo, are insufficient to withstand the enemy.

units.zh: 令軍器監造三萬具赴北京、澶定州。」
units.en: The Directorate of Military Equipment was ordered to forge thirty thousand sets and deliver them to Beijing and Chanzhou."
units.literal: An order directed the Directorate of Military Equipment to make thirty thousand sets and send them to Beijing and Chanzhou."

units.zh: 又令計河北所少兵器製造，其不急者毋得妄費材力。
units.en: The court also ordered an inventory of Hebei's shortfalls in arms, forbidding wasteful production of non-urgent items.
units.literal: Also ordered to calculate what weapons Hebei lacked and manufacture them; items not urgent must not waste materials and labor wantonly.

units.zh: 又詔民戶馬死，舊不以報官者並報，輸皮筋以充用。
units.en: Another edict required reporting horse deaths even when owners had previously failed to register them, and delivering hides and sinew for state use.
units.literal: Another edict: when commoners' horses died, those who had not reported to the authorities were also to report, and deliver hide and sinew for use.

units.zh: 帝慮置監未有實效，而虛用材役，詔中書、樞密院核實其事，令條畫以聞。
units.en: Fearing the new directorate achieved little while consuming labor and materials, the emperor ordered the Central Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs to investigate and report detailed findings.
units.literal: The emperor feared that establishing the directorate had no real effect while wasting materials and labor; he ordered the Central Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs to verify the facts and memorialize with detailed plans.

units.zh: 軍器監奏，置監以來，增造兵器若干，為工若干，視前器增而工省。
units.en: The directorate reported increased output since its founding, claiming more weapons with less labor than before.
units.literal: The Directorate of Military Equipment memorialized that since its establishment it had increased weapons production by such-and-such amounts, with such-and-such labor, weapons increased compared with before while labor was saved.

units.zh: 帝復詰之，且令與御前工作所較工孰省，驗器孰良。
units.en: The emperor pressed further, demanding a comparison with the Imperial Workshop on cost and quality.
units.literal: The emperor questioned this again and ordered comparison with the Imperial Workshop to see which saved more labor and which produced better gear.

units.zh: 王韶謂：「如此，恐內外相傾成俗。
units.en: Wang Shao warned: "Such comparisons will entrench rivalry between inner and outer agencies.
units.literal: Wang Shao said: "If it goes like this, I fear inner and outer offices will form a habit of mutual rivalry.

units.zh: 且往年軍器監檢察內臣折剝弓弩，隙由此生。
units.en: Years earlier the directorate had investigated eunuchs' abuses in bow production, breeding lasting hostility.
units.literal: Moreover in former years the Directorate of Military Equipment inspected inner eunuchs' exploitation of bows and crossbows, and enmity arose from that gap.

units.zh: 今令內臣較按軍器監，又如曩日相傾無已。」
units.en: Now putting eunuchs in charge of auditing the directorate would revive that endless infighting."
units.literal: Now ordering inner eunuchs to audit the Directorate of Military Equipment is again like the old days of endless mutual rivalry."

units.zh: 帝曰：「比累累說軍器監事，若不較見事實，即中外便以為聽小臣譖訴。
units.en: The emperor replied: "You keep raising this issue; without a factual comparison, everyone will assume the court heeds petty slander.
units.literal: The emperor said: "You have repeatedly spoken of Directorate of Military Equipment affairs; if we do not compare and see the facts, inner and outer will think the court listens to petty officials' slanders.

units.zh: 今令得實行法，所以明曲直也。」
units.en: An impartial comparison will clarify who is right and who is wrong."
units.literal: Now ordering the facts obtained and the law applied is to clarify right and wrong."

units.zh: 安石曰：「誠當如此。
units.en: Wang Anshi said: "That is exactly right.
units.literal: An Shi said: "It truly should be so.

units.zh: 若每事分別曲直，明其信誕，使功罪不蔽，則天下之治久矣。」
units.en: If every dispute were judged on its merits, trust and deceit exposed, and merit and guilt never hidden, good governance would endure."
units.literal: If in each matter right and wrong are separately distinguished, trust and deceit made clear, so merit and guilt are not concealed, then governance of the realm will long endure."

units.zh: 王韶曰：「軍器監事不須比較。」
units.en: Wang Shao said: "Directorate affairs need not be compared."
units.literal: Wang Shao said: "Directorate of Military Equipment affairs need not be compared.

units.zh: 帝曰：「事不比較，無由見枉直。」
units.en: The emperor countered: "Without comparison, truth and falsehood cannot be known."
units.literal: The emperor said: "Without comparison in affairs, there is no way to see crooked and straight."

units.zh: 安石曰：「朝廷治事，唯欲直而已。」
units.en: Wang Anshi added: "The court seeks only fairness in governance."
units.literal: An Shi said: "In governing affairs the court only wishes for straightness.

units.zh: 其後，安石卒以辯口解帝之疑，而軍器監獲免欺冒之罪。
units.en: In the end Wang Anshi's rhetoric dispelled the emperor's doubts, and the directorate escaped charges of fraud.
units.literal: Later, An Shi finally used eloquence to resolve the emperor's doubts, and the Directorate of Military Equipment escaped the crime of fraud.

units.zh: 冬十月，軍器監欲下河東等路采市曲木為鞍橋，帝以勞民費財，不許。
units.en: That winter the directorate sought to requisition curved timber for saddle frames across Hedong and other circuits; the emperor refused as an imposition on the people.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter, the Directorate of Military Equipment wished to send orders to Hedong and other circuits to purchase and collect curved timber for saddle bridges; the emperor, considering it a burden on the people and waste of wealth, did not permit it.

units.zh: 是時，河東、陝西、廣南帥臣邀功不已，請增給兵器，帝各令給與之。
units.en: Frontier commanders in Hedong, Shaanxi, and Guangnan, eager for glory, repeatedly requested more weapons and received them.
units.literal: At that time frontier commanders of Hedong, Shaanxi, and Guangnan ceaselessly sought merit and asked for increased arms; the emperor ordered each to be supplied.

units.zh: 至是，有乞以耕牛博買器甲者。
units.en: Some petitioners even sought to barter plow oxen for arms and armor.
units.literal: At this time some asked to trade plow oxen to buy weapons and armor.

units.zh: 元豐元年冬，鄜延路經略使呂惠卿乞給新樣刀，軍器監欲下江、浙、福建路製造，帝不許，給以內南庫短刃刀五萬五千口。
units.en: In the winter of the first year of Yuanfeng, Lü Huiqing on the Fuyan frontier requested new-style sabers; when the directorate proposed manufacturing them in the southeast, the emperor refused and issued fifty-five thousand short blades from the inner southern depot instead.
units.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yuanfeng, Fuyan frontier commissioner Lü Huiqing requested new-pattern blades; the Directorate of Military Equipment wished to order Jiang, Zhe, and Fujian circuits to manufacture them; the emperor did not permit it and instead granted fifty-five thousand short blades from the inner southern depot.

units.zh: 二年，御批有曰：「河東路見運物材於緣邊造軍器，顯為迂費張皇，可令軍器監速罷之。」
units.en: In the second year an imperial note read: "Hedong is shipping materials to border workshops to make weapons—clearly wasteful; order the Directorate of Military Equipment to halt this at once."
units.literal: In the second year, an imperial annotation read: "The Hedong circuit is now shipping materials to the border to make weapons—clearly wasteful exaggeration; order the Directorate of Military Equipment to halt this quickly."

units.zh: 三年，吉州奏：「奉詔市箭笴三十萬，非土地所產，且民間不素蓄，乞豫給緡錢，期以一年和市。」
units.en: Jizhou reported: "By edict we are to purchase thirty thousand arrow shafts, but they are not locally produced and the people do not stock them; we beg advance cash payment, with a one-year term to buy on the market."
units.literal: In the third year, Jizhou memorialized: "Obeying the edict to purchase thirty thousand arrow shafts, they are not products of this region and the people do not habitually stock them; we beg advance cash payment and a one-year term to purchase on the market."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The request was approved.
units.literal: Approved.

units.zh: 時西邊用兵久不解。
units.en: Western campaigns had by then become protracted.
units.literal: At that time warfare on the western frontier dragged on without resolution.

units.zh: 四年春，陝西轉運使李稷奏：「本道九軍，什物之外，一皆無之，乞於永興軍庫以餘財立法營辦。」
units.en: In the spring of the fourth year Li Ji, Shaanxi transport commissioner, reported: "This circuit's nine armies lack everything beyond sundries; we beg to use surplus funds in the Yongxing Army depot to establish regulations and provide for them."
units.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Shaanxi transport commissioner Li Ji memorialized: "In this circuit's nine armies, aside from sundries, everything else is lacking; we beg to use surplus funds in the Yongxing Army depot to establish regulations and provide for them by law."

units.zh: 七月，涇原路奏修渭州城畢，而防城戰具寡少，乞給三弓八牛床子弩、一槍三劍箭，各欲依法式製造。
units.en: In the seventh month Jingyuan reported Weizhou's walls repaired but defensive weapons scarce, requesting three-bow eight-ox bed crossbows and one-spear three-sword bolts made to standard patterns.
units.literal: In the seventh month, the Jingyuan circuit memorialized that repair of Weizhou's walls was complete but defensive battle gear was scant; it begged three-bow eight-ox bed crossbows and one-spear three-sword bolts, each to be made according to the legal pattern.

units.zh: 詔圖樣給之。
units.en: The court sent pattern diagrams.
units.literal: An edict granted diagram patterns.

units.zh: 五年七月，鄜延路計議邊事所奏乞緡錢百萬、工匠千人、鐵生熟五萬斤、牛馬皮萬張造軍器，並給之。
units.en: In the seventh month of the fifth year the Fuyan planning office requested one million cash, a thousand artisans, fifty thousand jin of iron, and ten thousand hides for arms production—all were granted.
units.literal: In the fifth year, seventh month, the Fuyan circuit Border Affairs Planning Office memorialized begging one million cash, a thousand craftsmen, fifty thousand jin of raw and wrought iron, and ten thousand ox and horse hides to make military gear—all were granted.

units.zh: 八月，詔令沈括以劈陣大斧五千選給西邊諸將。
units.en: In the eighth month Shen Kuo was ordered to distribute five thousand formation-splitting great axes to western commanders.
units.literal: In the eighth month, an edict ordered Shen Kuo to select five thousand formation-splitting great axes and distribute them to western frontier generals.

units.zh: 十一月，陝西轉運使李察言：「本路都作院五，宜各委監司提舉。」
units.en: In the eleventh month Li Cha, Shaanxi transport commissioner, said: "This circuit has five manufacturing offices; each should be placed under circuit supervisory oversight."
units.literal: In the eleventh month, Shaanxi transport commissioner Li Cha said: "This circuit has five directorate manufacturing offices; each should be placed under circuit supervisors' oversight."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Approved.
units.literal: Approved.

units.zh: 六年二月，詔：熙河路守具有闕，給氈三千領、牛皮萬張，運送之。
units.en: In the second month of the sixth year the Xihe circuit received three thousand felt blankets and ten thousand ox hides for deficient garrison gear.
units.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, an edict: where defensive gear on the Xihe circuit was lacking, grant three thousand felt blankets and ten thousand ox hides and transport them.

units.zh: 八月，從環慶路趙禼之請，以神臂弓一千、箭十萬給之。
units.en: In the eighth month, at Zhao Xie's request, Huanqing received one thousand divine-arm crossbows and one hundred thousand arrows.
units.literal: In the eighth month, at Zhao Zhi's request on the Huanqing circuit, one thousand divine-arm crossbows and one hundred thousand arrows were granted.

units.zh: 未幾，賜蘭會路藥箭二十五萬。
units.en: Soon afterward the Lanzhou-Hui circuit received two hundred fifty thousand poisoned arrows.
units.literal: Before long, the Lanzhou-Hui circuit was granted two hundred fifty thousand poisoned arrows.

units.zh: 七年，陝西轉運副使葉康直言：「秦鳳路軍器見闕名物計四百三十餘萬，使一一為之，非十餘年可就，乞自京給賜。」
units.en: In the seventh year Ye Kangzhi reported: "Qinfeng military gear is short more than 4.3 million named items; to make each locally would take more than ten years; we beg grants from the capital."
units.literal: In the seventh year, Shaanxi vice transport commissioner Ye Kangzhi said: "Qinfeng circuit military gear presently short by name-item counts totaling more than four million three hundred thousand; to make each one would take more than ten years; we beg grant from the capital."

units.zh: 詔量給之。
units.en: The court ordered grants in measured amounts.
units.literal: An edict ordered measured grants.

units.zh: 帝性儉約。
units.en: The emperor was frugal by nature.
units.literal: The emperor's nature was frugal and restrained.

units.zh: 有司造將官皮甲，欲以生絲染紅，代犛牛尾為瀝水，帝惜之，代以他毛。
units.en: When officials proposed dyeing raw silk red instead of yak-tail lacquer on generals' leather armor, the emperor economized and substituted other hair.
units.literal: When responsible offices made generals' leather armor and wished to dye raw silk red in place of yak-tail lacquer finish, the emperor prized it and substituted other hair.

units.zh: 於一弓、一矢、一甲、一牌之用，無不盡心焉。
units.en: He scrutinized every bow, arrow, suit of armor, and shield.
units.literal: For the use of one bow, one arrow, one armor, one shield—none was without his utmost care.

units.zh: 弓曰闊閃促張弓，罷長肖舊法。
units.en: Bows were redesigned as "wide-flash quick-draw" models, abandoning the old long-prod method.
units.literal: The bow was called the wide-flash quick-draw bow, abolishing the old long-prod method.

units.zh: 矢曰減指箭。
units.en: Arrows became "reduced-finger" types.
units.literal: Arrows were called reduced-finger arrows.

units.zh: 牌以欒竹穿皮為之，以易桐木牌。
units.en: Shields of catalpa bamboo and leather replaced paulownia wood.
units.literal: Shields were made of catalpa bamboo pierced with leather, replacing paulownia wood shields.

units.zh: 改素鐵甲為編挨甲。
units.en: Plain iron armor gave way to linked lamellar armor.
units.literal: Plain iron armor was changed to linked-lamellar armor.

units.zh: 其法精密，乃劉昌祚、尹抃、閻守勤等所定制度云。
units.en: These refinements formed the code devised by Liu Changzuo, Yin Bian, Yan Shouqin, and others.
units.literal: These methods were precise and fine—it was the regulatory system fixed by Liu Changzuo, Yin Bian, Yan Shouqin, and others.

units.zh: 八年十月，詔內外所造軍器，以見餘物材工匠造之，兵匠、民工即罷遣之。
units.en: In the tenth month of the eighth year an edict required using surplus materials and labor for arms production and dismissing conscripted craftsmen.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year, an edict: military gear made within and without should use surplus materials, craftsmen, and leftover stock; armorer-soldiers and civilian laborers were to be dismissed.

units.zh: 元祐元年，詔：三路既罷保甲團教，其器甲各送官收貯，勿得以破損拘民整治。
units.en: In Yuanyou 1 an edict ordered baojia weapons surrendered to officials for storage without forcing civilians to repair damaged pieces.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, an edict: since the three circuits had abolished baojia militia drill, their weapons and armor were each to be delivered to officials for storage; they must not use damage as pretext to constrain the people to repair them.

units.zh: 八月，詔太僕少卿高遵惠，會工部及軍器監內外作坊及諸州都作院工器之數，以要切軍器立為歲課，務得中道，他非要切，並權住勿造。
units.en: In the eighth month Gao Zunhui was ordered to survey workshops nationwide, set moderate annual quotas for essential arms, and suspend nonessential production.
units.literal: In the eighth month, an edict to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Gao Zunhui to convene with the Ministry of Works and the Directorate of Military Equipment, inner and outer workshops and prefectural manufacturing offices, on weapon counts, establishing annual quotas for essential military gear at a moderate level; other non-essential items were temporarily halted.

units.zh: 於是數年之間，督責少弛。
units.en: For several years enforcement slackened.
units.literal: Thereupon over several years supervisory pressure was somewhat relaxed.

units.zh: 紹聖三年，有司言：「州郡兵備，全為虛文，恐緩急不足備禦。
units.en: In Shaosheng 3 officials warned: "Prefectural military preparedness is entirely empty form; we fear that in emergency it will be insufficient for defense.
units.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, responsible offices said: "Prefectural military preparedness is entirely empty form; we fear that in emergency it will be insufficient for defense.

units.zh: 請稍推行熙寧之詔，常令封樁、排垛，依雜隊法。」
units.en: They asked to revive Xining rules requiring sealed, stacked stores per the miscellaneous-company regulations."
units.literal: We beg slightly to implement the Xining edicts, regularly requiring sealing, stacking, and arrangement according to the miscellaneous-company law."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Approved.
units.literal: Approved.

units.zh: 元符元年，詔江、湖、淮、浙六路合造神臂弓三千、箭三十萬。
units.en: In Yuanfu 1 the six southeastern circuits were ordered to produce three thousand divine-arm crossbows and three hundred thousand arrows.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, an edict ordered the six circuits of Jiang, Hu, Huai, and Zhe jointly to make three thousand divine-arm crossbows and three hundred thousand arrows.

units.zh: 二年，臣僚奏乞增造神臂弓，於是軍器監所造歲益千餘弓。
units.en: In the second year officials requested more divine-arm crossbows, raising annual directorate output by over a thousand.
units.literal: In the second year, officials memorialized begging increased divine-arm crossbow production; thereupon the Directorate of Military Equipment's annual output increased by more than a thousand bows.

units.zh: 是歲，詔河北沿邊州城壁、樓櫓、器械、各務修治，有不治者罪之。
units.en: That year Hebei frontier walls, towers, and weapons had to be repaired under penalty.
units.literal: That year, an edict ordered Hebei frontier prefectures' walls, towers, and gear each to be repaired; those who failed were punished.

units.zh: 先是，二廣路土丁令依熙寧指揮修置器械。
units.en: Earlier, native troops in the two Guang circuits had been ordered under Xining rules to maintain arms.
units.literal: Earlier, the two Guang circuits' native levies were ordered under Xining directives to equip and maintain weapons.

units.zh: 三年，知端州蕭元刂上疏，極言傷財害民，其弊非一，乞住買槍手器械。
units.en: In the third year Xiao Yuanzhang of Duanzhou memorialized that arms procurement inflicted many abuses on the people and begged to stop buying musketeer equipment.
units.literal: In the third year, Duanzhou prefect Xiao Yuanzhang memorialized at length that it harmed the treasury and injured the people, the abuses not one; he begged to halt purchase of musketeer gear.

units.zh: 疏奏不報。
units.en: The throne did not reply.
units.literal: The memorial was submitted but no response was given.

units.zh: 崇寧初，臣僚爭言元祐以來因循弛廢，兵不犀利。
units.en: Early in Chongning officials blamed Yuanyou-era laxity for dull weapons.
units.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, officials contended that since Yuanyou there had been laxity and neglect, and troops lacked sharp weapons.

units.zh: 詔復令諸路都作院創造修治，官吏考察一如熙寧時矣。
units.en: An edict restored Xining-style manufacture, repair, and official inspection on every circuit.
units.literal: An edict restored orders for circuit manufacturing offices to create and repair, with official assessment as in Xining times.

units.zh: 時有詔造五十將器械，從工部請，令內外共造，由是都大提舉內外製造軍器所之名立焉。
units.en: When fifty commands needed new gear, joint inner-outer production created the Grand Directorate for Military Equipment Manufacture.
units.literal: At that time an edict ordered manufacture of gear for fifty commands; following the Ministry of Works' request, inner and outer offices were to manufacture jointly; hence the name Grand Directorate for Inner and Outer Manufacture of Military Equipment was established.

units.zh: 初，從邢恕之議，下令創造兵車數十乘，買牛以駕。
units.en: Earlier, on Xing Shu's advice, dozens of war chariots were built and oxen purchased to haul them.
units.literal: Earlier, following Xing Shu's proposal, an order was issued to create several dozen war chariots and buy oxen to draw them.

units.zh: 已而蔡碩又請河北置五十將兵器，且為兵車萬乘。
units.en: Cai Shuo then proposed Hebei arms for fifty commands plus ten thousand chariots.
units.literal: Then Cai Shuo also requested Hebei gear for fifty commands and moreover ten thousand war chariots.

units.zh: 蔡京主其說，奸吏旁緣而因為民害者深矣。
units.en: Cai Jing backed the schemes, and corrupt underlings inflicted grave harm on the populace.
units.literal: Cai Jing championed these plans, and corrupt clerks on the margins thereby became deep harm to the people.

units.zh: 崇寧三年，河北、陝西都轉運司言：「兵車之式，若用許彥圭所定，則車大而費倍。
units.en: In Chongning 3 the Hebei and Shaanxi transport commissions reported: "If Xu Yangui's chariot pattern is used, the chariot is large and cost doubles.
units.literal: In the third year of Chongning, the Hebei and Shaanxi transport commissions said: "For the war-chariot pattern, if Xu Yankui's design is used, the chariot is large and cost doubles.

units.zh: 若依往年二十將舊式，則輕小易用，且可省費。」
units.en: They favored the lighter legacy pattern to save expense."
units.literal: If following the former twenty-command old pattern of recent years, it is light and easy to use and costs can be saved."

units.zh: 詔卒以許彥圭式行之。
units.en: The court nonetheless adopted Xu Yangui's design.
units.literal: An edict finally ordered Xu Yankui's pattern implemented.

units.zh: 時熙河轉運副使李復先奏曰：「今之用兵，與古不同。
units.en: Xihe vice commissioner Li Fu argued: "Warfare today differs from antiquity.
units.literal: At that time Xihe vice transport commissioner Li Fu first memorialized: "Warfare today differs from antiquity.

units.zh: 古者征戰有禮，不為詭遇，多由正途，故車可行而敵不敢輕犯。
units.en: Ancient warfare followed ritualized routes where chariots could move safely.
units.literal: In antiquity campaigns had ritual; no treacherous encounters; mostly by proper routes—thus chariots could travel and the enemy dared not lightly violate them.

units.zh: 今之用兵，盡在極邊，下砦駐軍，各以保險為利，車不能上。
units.en: Today fighting occurs on rugged frontiers where chariots cannot climb to stockaded posts.
units.literal: Warfare today is entirely on the extreme frontier; garrisons in stockades, each taking rugged terrain as advantage—chariots cannot ascend.

units.zh: 又戰陣之交，一進一退，車不能及，一被追襲，遂非己有。
units.en: In fluid battle chariots cannot advance or retreat with infantry and are easily captured.
units.literal: Moreover in the clash of battle lines, one advance one retreat—chariots cannot keep up; once pursued and attacked, they are no longer one's own.

units.zh: 臣屢觀戎馬之間，雖糧糗、衣服、器械不能為用，況於車乎？
units.en: I have seen even food, clothing, and weapons fail on campaign—chariots are far less useful.
units.literal: Your servant has repeatedly observed among barbarian horses that though grain, clothes, and weapons cannot be used, how much less chariots?

units.zh: 臣聞此車之造，許彥圭因姚麟以進其說。
units.en: These chariots reached the court through Yao Lin promoting Xu Yangui's design.
units.literal: Your servant hears this chariot's manufacture: Xu Yankui, through Yao Lin, advanced his plan.

units.zh: 朝廷以麟熟於邊事，而不知彥圭輕妄、麟立私恩以誤國計。
units.en: The court trusted Lin's frontier expertise, not realizing Yangui was reckless and Lin acted from private loyalty.
units.literal: The court, because Lin was familiar with frontier affairs, did not know Yankui was reckless and Lin established private favor to mislead state planning.

units.zh: 其車比於常法闊六七寸，運不合轍，東來兵夫牽免不行，以致典賣衣物，自賃牛具，終日而進六七里，棄車而逃者往往而是。
units.en: The chariots were wider than standard tracks; draft animals failed; laborers sold belongings, hired oxen, advanced only six or seven li daily, and often abandoned the vehicles.
units.literal: The chariot compared with the usual method is six or seven inches wider; transport does not fit the ruts; eastern laborers leading it could not move it, so they sold clothing, hired oxen and gear themselves, advancing six or seven li in a whole day; those who abandoned the chariot and fled were often thus.

units.zh: 夫未造則有配買物材、顧差夫匠之擾；
units.en: Even before completion, requisitioning materials and craftsmen harassed the people;
units.literal: Before manufacture there was the disturbance of apportioned material purchases and hired craftsmen;

units.zh: 既成，又難運致，則為諸路之患有不可勝言者矣。
units.en: and after completion, transport proved impossible, burdening every circuit unbearably.
units.literal: once completed, transport was again difficult—the affliction to the circuits is beyond full description.

units.zh: 彥圭但圖一官之得，不知有誤於國，此而不誅，何以懲後！
units.en: Yangui sought only personal promotion at the state's expense; failure to punish him would invite repetition.
units.literal: Yankui only sought gain of one office, not knowing he erred against the state; if this is not punished, how can later men be warned!

units.zh: 今乞便行罷造，已造者不復運來，以寬民力。」
units.en: I beg to halt production immediately and not ship finished chariots, relieving the populace."
units.literal: Now we beg immediately to halt manufacture; those already made need not be transported here, to ease the people's strength."

units.zh: 其後，彥圭卒得罪。
units.en: Yangui was eventually punished.
units.literal: Later, Yankui finally was punished for his offense.

units.zh: 元豐之時，河北、河東路軍器，每季終委逐路職司更互考察。
units.en: Under Yuanfeng, Hebei and Hedong arms were inspected quarterly by rotating circuit officials.
units.literal: During Yuanfeng times, Hebei and Hedong circuit military gear at each season's end was entrusted to circuit officials in rotation for inspection.

units.zh: 元祐罷之。
units.en: Yuanyou abolished the practice.
units.literal: Yuanyou abolished this.

units.zh: 四年，因工部之請，復行之。
units.en: In the fourth year the Ministry of Works restored it.
units.literal: In the fourth year, at the Ministry of Works' request, it was restored.

units.zh: 大觀二年，手詔曰：「前東南備禦指揮，深慮監郡縣吏急切者倚法害民，廢職者慢令失事，如築城壁、造軍器、收戰馬、習水戰之類，並可量度工力，計以歲月，漸次興作，毋得急遽科斂及差雇百姓，使急不擾民，緩不廢事，然後為稱。」
units.en: In Daguan 2 an imperial handwritten edict declared: "The former southeastern defense directive deeply feared that harsh supervising prefectural and county clerks would harm the people by relying on the law, while negligent officials would lose affairs by slackening orders—such as building walls, making military gear, collecting war horses, and practicing naval warfare—all could measure labor, calculate by months, and be undertaken gradually; they must not urgently levy and conscript the people, so that urgency does not disturb the people and slackness does not neglect affairs—then it may be called fitting."
units.literal: In the second year of Daguan, an imperial handwritten edict said: "The former southeastern defense directive deeply feared that supervising prefectural and county clerks who were harsh would harm the people by relying on the law, while those who neglected duty would lose affairs by slackening orders—such as building walls, making military gear, collecting war horses, practicing naval warfare—all could measure labor power, calculate by months, and gradually undertake them; they must not urgently levy and conscript the people; so that urgency does not disturb the people and slackness does not neglect affairs—then it may be called fitting."

units.zh: 尋詔限十年一切畢工。
units.en: A follow-up edict allowed ten years for full completion.
units.literal: Shortly an edict limited ten years for everything to be completed.

units.zh: 四月，罷黎、雅等州市犛牛尾，慮為民害。
units.en: In the fourth month yak-tail markets in Li, Ya, and related prefectures were closed as harmful to the people.
units.literal: In the fourth month, market purchase of yak tails in Li, Ya, and other prefectures was abolished, fearing harm to the people.

units.zh: 八月，提舉御前軍器所奏，乞如崇寧五年指揮，下諸路買牛角四十萬隻、筋十萬斤。
units.en: In the eighth month the Imperial Military Equipment Directorate requested circuit purchases of four hundred thousand ox horns and one hundred thousand jin of sinew per Chongning rules.
units.literal: In the eighth month, the Imperial Military Equipment Directorate memorialized begging, per the Chongning fifth-year directive, to order circuits to buy four hundred thousand ox horns and one hundred thousand jin of sinew.

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Approved.
units.literal: Approved.

units.zh: 政和二年二月，詔諸路州郡造軍器有不用熙寧法式者，有司議罰，具為令。
units.en: In the second month of Zhenghe 2 an edict penalized prefectures that ignored Xining weapon patterns.
units.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhenghe, an edict: where prefectures made military gear not using the Xining pattern, responsible offices were to deliberate punishment and draw up regulations.

units.zh: 六月，又詔並用御前軍器所降法式，前二月指揮勿行。
units.en: In the sixth month all production was ordered to follow Imperial Directorate patterns, superseding the February directive.
units.literal: In the sixth month, another edict ordered unified use of patterns sent down from the Imperial Military Equipment Directorate; the directive of the second month before was not to be implemented.

units.zh: 三年，詔：「馬甲曩用黑髹漆，今易以朱。」
units.en: In the third year an edict declared: "Horse armor formerly used black lacquer; now change it to cinnabar red."
units.literal: In the third year, an edict: "Horse armor formerly used black lacquer; now change to cinnabar.

units.zh: 是歲，姚古奏更定軍器，曩時甲二副，今拆造三副；
units.en: That year Yao Gu revised standards: where two armor sets had been issued, three lighter sets were now made from the same materials;
units.literal: That year, Yao Gu memorialized revising military gear: formerly two suits of armor, now dismantle and make three;

units.zh: 曩時手刀太重，今皆令輕便易用；
units.en: hand blades were lightened for ease of use;
units.literal: formerly hand blades were too heavy, now all were ordered light and easy to use;

units.zh: 曩時神臂弓硾二石三斗，今硾一石四斗。
units.en: and divine-arm crossbow draw weight fell from 2.3 to 1.4 stone.
units.literal: formerly the divine-arm crossbow drew two stone three dou, now draws one stone four dou.

units.zh: 從之，悉下諸路改造。
units.en: The changes were approved and ordered remanufactured on every circuit.
units.literal: Approved; all were sent down to the circuits for remanufacture.

units.zh: 六年，軍器少監鄧之綱奏：「國家諸路為將一百三十有一，訓練士卒，各給軍器，以備不虞。
units.en: In the sixth year Deng Zhigang, vice director of military equipment, noted: "The state has 131 commands nationwide, training soldiers and supplying each with military gear against the unforeseen.
units.literal: In the sixth year, Vice Director of Military Equipment Deng Zhigang memorialized: "The state's circuits have one hundred thirty-one commands, training soldiers, each supplied with military gear against the unforeseen.

units.zh: 惟河北諸將軍器乃熙、豐時造，精利牢密，冠於諸路。
units.en: Hebei alone still held Xi-Feng-era gear, the finest in the empire.
units.literal: Only Hebei's command gear was made in the Xi and Feng era, refined, sharp, and solid, surpassing all circuits.

units.zh: 臣恐歲久因循，多致損弊。
units.en: I fear years of neglect have left much of it damaged.
units.literal: Your servant fears that over years of routine, much will fall to damage and decay.

units.zh: 乞自河北、陝西路為首，令諸路一新戎器，仰稱陛下追述先誌，儲戎器、壯國威之意。」
units.en: I beg to begin renewing arms in Hebei and Shaanxi, then nationwide, to fulfill Your Majesty's aim of restoring stores and national strength."
units.literal: We beg starting with Hebei and Shaanxi circuits to order every circuit to renew frontier gear anew, upholding Your Majesty's intent to follow the former exemplar, store military gear, and strengthen national might."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: Approved.
units.literal: Approved.

units.zh: 七年，之綱三上奏，一言修武庫，二言整軍器，大省國用。
units.en: In the seventh year Deng Zhigang submitted three memorials on arsenal repair and arms standardization, claiming major savings.
units.literal: In the seventh year, Zhigang memorialized three times—one word on repairing the arsenal, two words on putting military gear in order, greatly saving state expenditures.

units.zh: 詔升之綱為大監，又遷一官。
units.en: He was promoted to grand director of the directorate and advanced one rank.
units.literal: An edict promoted Zhigang to grand director and also advanced him one rank.

units.zh: 時宇文粹中賜對崇政殿，奏武庫事，因奏：「武庫有祖宗所御軍器十餘色，乞編入《鹵簿圖志》，遇郊兵重禮，陳於儀物之首，以識武功，且示不忘創業艱難意。」
units.en: Yuwen Cuizhong, granted audience in Chongzheng Hall, memorialized: "The arsenal has more than ten types of military gear used by the ancestors; we beg they be compiled into the Halberd Escort Illustrated Record and displayed at the head of suburban ritual processions to mark martial achievement and show intent not to forget the hardship of founding the enterprise."
units.literal: At that time Yuwen Cuizhong was granted audience in Chongzheng Hall and memorialized on arsenal affairs, also memorializing: "The arsenal has more than ten types of military gear used by the ancestors; we beg they be compiled into the Halberd Escort Illustrated Record; when suburban troops perform heavy rites, display them at the head of ritual objects to mark martial achievement and show intent not to forget the hardship of founding the enterprise."

units.zh: 是年，御筆以武庫當修軍器近一億萬，其中箭鏃五千餘萬，用平時工料，須七十年餘然後可畢。
units.en: That year an imperial note estimated nearly 100 million arsenal items needing repair, including 50 million arrowheads—a seventy-year task at normal pace.
units.literal: That year, an imperial brush-note said the arsenal should repair nearly one hundred million military items, among them more than fifty million arrowheads; using peacetime labor and materials, it would take more than seventy years to finish.

units.zh: 於是令鄧之綱分給沿流作院，限三年修之，而權住三年上供軍器。
units.en: Deng Zhigang was told to spread repairs among riverside workshops over three years while suspending circuit tribute arms for three years.
units.literal: Thereupon Deng Zhigang was ordered to distribute to workshops along the rivers, limiting repair to three years, while temporarily halting three years of tribute arms from the circuits.

units.zh: 八年，以之綱奏，諸路歲起上供料買分數，特免三年綱發。
units.en: In the eighth year circuit tribute procurement quotas were waived for three years on his recommendation.
units.literal: In the eighth year, at Zhigang's memorial, the circuits' annual tribute procurement quotas were specially exempted from collection for three years.

units.zh: 然自時厥後，申明郡縣牛皮角筋之禁，紛然為害者，之綱之請也。
units.en: Yet his request also led to renewed, harmful prohibitions on local ox hide, horn, and sinew.
units.literal: Yet from that time onward, clarifying the prohibition on ox hide, horn, and sinew in prefectures and counties became a widespread harm—it was Zhigang's request.

units.zh: 宣和元年，權荊湖南路提點刑獄公事鄭濟奏：「本路惟潭、邵二州，各有年額製造軍器。
units.en: In Xuanhe 1 Zheng Ji, acting judicial commissioner on the Jinghu South circuit, reported: "This circuit has only Tan and Shao prefectures, each with an annual quota for manufacturing military gear.
units.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, Acting Jinghu South Circuit Judicial Commissioner Zheng Ji memorialized: "This circuit has only Tan and Shao two prefectures, each with annual quotas for manufacturing military gear.

units.zh: 今年製造已足，躬親試驗，並依法式，不誤施用。」
units.en: This year's output was complete; he had tested it personally and found it met legal patterns."
units.literal: This year's manufacture is already sufficient; I personally tested it, all according to the legal pattern, not mistaken in application."

units.zh: 詔加旌賞，以為諸路之勸。
units.en: The court rewarded him as an example to other circuits.
units.literal: An edict added commendation and reward, taking this as encouragement for all circuits.

units.zh: 然自是歲督軍器率用御筆處分，工造不已而較數嘗闕，繕修無虛歲而每稱弊壞。
units.en: Thereafter annual arms quotas followed imperial brush orders: workshops labored endlessly yet counts fell short, repairs never ceased yet gear was always reported ruined.
units.literal: Yet from this time annual supervision of military gear mostly used imperial brush directives; craftsmen worked unceasingly yet tallies were often short; repair had no year without work yet each year was called damaged.

units.zh: 大抵中外相應，一以虛文，上下相蒙，而馴致靖康之禍矣。
units.en: Court and countryside alike kept up empty paperwork until the Jingkang catastrophe.
units.literal: In general inner and outer corresponded in empty form; upper and lower deceived one another, and thus they drifted into the disaster of Jingkang.

units.zh: 靖康初，兵仗皆闕，詔書屢下，嚴立賞刑，而卒亦無補。
units.en: When Jingkang began, armories were bare; repeated edicts with harsh penalties still failed.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, weapons were all lacking; edicts were repeatedly issued with strict rewards and punishments, yet in the end it availed nothing.

units.zh: 時通判河陽、權州事張旂奏曰：「河陽自今春以來，累有軍馬經過，軍士舉隨身軍器若馬甲、神臂弓、箭槍牌之類，於市肆博易熟食，名為寄頓，其實棄遣，避逃征役。
units.en: Zhang Qi, acting prefect of Heyang, reported: "Since this spring Heyang has repeatedly had armies pass through; soldiers trade personal gear such as horse armor, divine-arm crossbows, arrows, spears, and shields in markets for cooked food, claiming temporary storage while actually abandoning them to evade corvée service.
units.literal: At that time Zhang Qi, vice-prefect of Heyang and acting prefect, memorialized: "Heyang since this spring has repeatedly had armies pass through; soldiers take personal gear such as horse armor, divine-arm crossbows, arrows, spears, and shields to trade in markets for cooked food, called 'temporary deposit,' but in fact abandon them to evade corvée and campaign service.

units.zh: 拘收三日間，得器械四千二百餘物。
units.en: In three days officials seized more than 4,200 abandoned weapons.
units.literal: Within three days of seizure, four thousand two hundred odd items of gear were obtained.

units.zh: 此乃太原援師，尚且棄捐器甲，則他路軍馬事勢可知。
units.en: Even Taiyuan relief troops discarded their arms, revealing how desperate other armies had become.
units.literal: These were Taiyuan relief troops, yet they still cast off weapons and armor—then the situation of army troops on other routes can be known.

units.zh: 宜諭民首納，免貽他患。」
units.en: He urged civilians to turn in abandoned gear before it caused further harm."
units.literal: It is fitting to instruct the people to surrender them first, lest other troubles be left behind."

units.zh: 帝善旂奏，賞以一官。
units.en: The emperor approved and promoted Zhang Qi one rank.
units.literal: The emperor approved Qi's memorial and rewarded him with one rank.

units.zh: 初，御前軍器監、軍器所萬全軍匠以三千七百為額，東、西作坊工匠以五千為額。
units.en: Originally the Imperial Military Equipment offices employed 3,700 Wanshan artisans and 5,000 workshop craftsmen.
units.literal: Earlier, the Imperial Military Equipment Directorate and Military Equipment Office's Wanshan Army artisans had a quota of three thousand seven hundred; the eastern and western workshops' artisans had a quota of five thousand.

units.zh: 紹興初，役兵才千人，久之，增至五千六百餘，又於諸道增二千九百餘，本券外復增給日錢百七十、月米七斗半。
units.en: Under Shaoxing corvée artisans rose from 1,000 to 5,600, with 2,900 more on the circuits plus extra daily cash and monthly rice.
units.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, corvée soldiers were only a thousand; after long time increased to more than five thousand six hundred; also on various routes added more than two thousand nine hundred; beyond base vouchers additionally granted daily cash one hundred seventy and monthly rice seven dou and a half.

units.zh: 於是內庫累歲兵械山積，而諸軍悉除戎器。
units.en: Inner depots overflowed with arms while field armies stripped their own equipment.
units.literal: Thereupon the inner depots year after year piled military gear like mountains, while the various armies all removed frontier weapons.

units.zh: 二十六年，詔：「工匠宜減免，江、浙、福建諸州物料悉蠲之。」
units.en: In the twenty-sixth year an edict declared: "Artisans should be reduced and exempted; material levies in Jiang, Zhe, and Fujian prefectures are all remitted."
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, an edict: "Artisans should be reduced and exempted; Jiang, Zhe, and Fujian prefectures' materials are all to be remitted."

units.zh: 有司奏物料減三之一，工匠二千、雜役兵五百為額。
units.en: Officials cut material quotas by one third and capped artisans at 2,000 plus 500 miscellaneous laborers.
units.literal: Responsible offices memorialized materials reduced by one third; artisans two thousand and miscellaneous corvée soldiers five hundred as quota.

units.zh: 舊，軍器所得專達。
units.en: Formerly arms shipments used dedicated transport.
units.literal: Formerly, military equipment receipts went through dedicated transport.

units.zh: 建炎中，嘗以閹官董愨提舉，尋罷之。
units.en: In the Jianyan era the eunuch Dong Que was briefly appointed supervisor then removed.
units.literal: During the Jianyan period, a eunuch Dong Kai was once appointed to supervise; soon abolished.

units.zh: 紹興五年，隸工部，後復以中人典領。
units.en: In Shaoxing 5 the office fell under the Ministry of Works, then again under eunuch management.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing, subordinated to the Ministry of Works; later again placed under a eunuch manager.

units.zh: 三十年，工部言非祖宗建官意，詔依條檢察。
units.en: In the thirtieth year the Ministry of Works protested that eunuch control violated ancestral intent and ordered a regulatory review.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Ministry of Works said this was not the intent of the ancestors in establishing offices; an edict ordered inspection according to regulations.

units.zh: 孝宗受禪，增提點官一員，御史力論其不可，復隸工部焉。
units.en: Xiaozong briefly added a supervisory post, but censors restored Ministry of Works jurisdiction.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the throne, one supervisory official was added; censors forcefully argued it was impermissible, and it was again subordinated to the Ministry of Works.

units.zh: 造車之制。
units.en: Regulations for Chariot Manufacture
units.literal: Regulations for making chariots.

units.zh: 渡江後，東南地多沮洳險隘，不以車為主。
units.en: After the southward retreat, marshy southeastern terrain made chariots impractical.
units.literal: After crossing the Yangzi, the southeast's terrain was mostly marshy, boggy, and narrow—chariots were not taken as primary.

units.zh: 宗澤、李綱有戰車法，王大智獻車式，皆不復用，而屬意甲胄、弧矢之利矣。
units.en: Methods of Zong Ze, Li Gang, and Wang Dazhi were abandoned in favor of armor and archery.
